steps.title: Calculate effluent dose
steps.body: Effluent rate (mL/hr) = replacement + dialysate + net ultrafiltration. Divide by patient weight for mL/kg/hr — the standard CRRT dose metric.
steps.tip: Example: 2100 mL/hr effluent in 100 kg = 21 mL/kg/hr.

steps.title: Target dose in AKI
steps.body: KDIGO-era data support ≥20–25 mL/kg/hr effluent for adequate solute clearance in most ICU patients. Under-dosing is a common cause of persistent uremia or refractory acidosis.
steps.tip: Higher doses may be needed for hypercatabolic states — reassess daily.

steps.title: Filtration fraction ≤ 20%
steps.body: FF = (pre-filter replacement + net UF) / blood flow. Keep ≤20% to reduce clotting and membrane fouling, especially with post-dilution hemofiltration.
steps.tip: If FF rises, increase blood flow or switch more replacement to pre-filter.

steps.title: Net fluid balance
steps.body: Match net ultrafiltration to volume status: overloaded patients need negative balance; euvolemic patients aim near zero; hypovolemic patients may need positive balance.
steps.tip: Reassess every 6 h: weights, I/O, hemodynamics, and lung ultrasound.
